senses.definition: One who carries out a theft.

quotes.reference: c. 1596–1598 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Merchant of Venice”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene iii]:

senses.definition: One who steals another person's property, especially by stealth and without using force or violence.

quotes.text: Take heed to false harlots, and more, ye wot what. / If noise ye heare, / Looke all be cleare: / Least drabs doe noie thee, / And theeues destroie thee.

senses.definition: (obsolete) A waster in the snuff of a candle.

quotes.text: But hear you, my Worthy Brethren: do not you, where you see a thief in the candle, call presently for an extinguisher[…]
